aiOverview.content: A potential "Super El Niño" is projected to develop by summer 2026 and last through the end of the year, with a one-in-three chance of becoming a "strong" event, potentially rivaling past, intense, and warm episodes. It threatens to bring extreme global weather shifts, including severe drought in some areas, intense flooding, and significantly increased global temperatures, threatening 2026 or 2027 with records. This video explains the formation of an El Niño event:44sNational Weather Service Alaska RegionYouTube• Mar 17, 2026 44s Key Forecast Details for 2026 Formation Timing: Emerging by summer 2026, with rapid development predicted after the collapse of the previous La Niña phase. Strength: There is a 62% chance of El Niño conditions developing by June-August 2026, with a 1-in-3 chance of it becoming a "strong" or "super" event by late 2026. Global Impacts: If a Super El Niño emerges, it is likely to cause massive disruptions, including intense rainfall in some regions and severe droughts in others. Temperature Record: While 2024 is currently expected to remain the warmest year, this 2026 event could make 2026 or 2027 a record-warm year due to the release of ocean heat. Hurricane Season: The event is expected to increase wind shear across the Atlantic, which typically reduces tropical storm formation in the second half of the 2026 hurricane season, though the risk of major hits remains. Regional Impacts Expected United States: Increased risk of severe weather and tornadoes, particularly in the Southeast. Global: Increased probability of warmer temperatures and higher impacts in early 2026 forecasts. Other areas: Potential impacts include disruption to the Indian monsoon and droughts in parts of the Pacific. This anticipated 2026 event follows the strong 2023-2024 El Niño.
